title: Kestrel and the Vow
premise: August Underhill has spent ten years ghostwriting other people's truths while burying her own—chief among them the vow she and rival memoirist Jonah Kestrel made one snowbound night in their twenties: that if they were ever brave enough, they'd find each other again. When both are hired to work on the same estate's centenary history—she secretly drafting the matriarch's memoirs, he writing his own family's rebuttal—a blizzard traps them together with a decade of unsaid words. As the inheritance dispute over the estate sharpens and August's ghostwriting contract forbids disclosure of what she knows, they must choose between professional survival and the sentence each has rehearsed for ten years. In the end, August publishes her first book under her own name—the truth about that night—and Jonah answers it in print, choosing love against every duty that kept them apart.
about_author: Marguerite Quintana is a former archivist who spent years cataloguing other people's love letters before writing her own stories. She lives in a converted mill town in Vermont, where the winters are long enough for second chances.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: August's POV. She finishes ghostwriting a celebrity memoir she'll never sign, establishing her invisibility as craft and armor. A new commission arrives from the Ashcombe estate. Beat: competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: August signs an ironclad NDA with the dying matriarch Vivian Ashcombe, who wants her true history recorded before her heirs rewrite it. Beat: the weight of secrets, and a hint Vivian knows more about August than expected.

chapters.title: The Rival's Byline
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He arrives at Ashcombe to write the Kestrel family's counter-history to Vivian's claims, resentful of the woman who vanished on him ten years ago. Beat: old wound reopened by a name on a guest ledger.

chapters.title: Snowfall at the Gate
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The storm closes the mountain road; August and Jonah come face to face in the great hall, both trapped, both pretending indifference. Beat: electric shock disguised as politeness.

chapters.title: Two Rooms, One Roof
chapters.summary: August's POV. Assigned adjacent rooms, they navigate corridors and small talk while cataloguing the library separately. Beat: proximity as slow torture.

chapters.title: What Vivian Remembers
chapters.summary: Vivian's dictated memories begin—her own lost love during the war, a man her family forbade. August hears her own future in the past tense. Beat: recognition and dread.

chapters.title: Chess by Firelight
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Storm-bound evenings force games of chess with August; banter becomes confession-adjacent. He learns she never married either. Beat: tenderness rekindling under sarcasm.

chapters.title: The Ledger of 2014
chapters.summary: August's POV. Flashback: the night of the original vow—young August and Jonah, one shared night, a promise to return to the boathouse in one year if brave enough. Neither came. Beat: the mistake defined.

chapters.title: Heirs and Apparitions
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Vivian's grandson Marcus arrives by snowcat, hostile to the memoir project and suspicious of both writers. Beat: external threat crystallizes; duty vs. truth takes shape.

chapters.title: Found Pages
chapters.summary: August's POV. In the archive she discovers letters proving Vivian's lost love was a Kestrel—the two families' feud is a broken romance. She now holds ammunition she shouldn't. Beat: knowledge as burden.

chapters.title: The Interview That Isn't
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He interviews Vivian officially; she deflects, testing him, asking pointed questions about whether he ever kept a promise. Beat: the matriarch as matchmaker and antagonist at once.

chapters.title: Thaw Lines
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Power flickers out; they share one candlelit kitchen, and almost say the rehearsed sentence. Interrupted by Marcus. Beat: near-confession, frustration.

chapters.title: Contract Clauses
chapters.summary: August's POV. Her NDA explicitly forbids revealing the memoir's contents—including the Kestrel letters—to anyone, Jonah included. Telling him would end her career. Beat: the trap tightens.

chapters.title: Boathouse in White
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He finds the derelict boathouse from their youth and realizes August has been here too—fresh footprints, a repaired latch. Hope he'd buried resurfaces. Beat: evidence of her heart.

chapters.title: Marcus's Offer
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. He offers Jonah a lucrative publishing deal if his book discredits Vivian's memory entirely. Jonah hesitates; money plus revenge versus the woman he loves. Beat: temptation.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Drafts
chapters.summary: August's POV. We see her secret folder: a novel begun the morning after the vow, revised yearly, always ending before the reunion scene because she can't imagine it honestly. Beat: art stunted by fear.

chapters.title: The Second Storm
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A worse storm knocks out heat; the household shelters in the east wing. Forced intimacy, blankets, Vivian telling war-era stories by lantern. Beat: community forming around the two rivals.

chapters.title: Vivian's Condition
chapters.summary: August's POV. Vivian's health fails sharply; she makes August swear the memoir will be published under August's real name, not a ghost's. 'Invisibility is a habit, dear, not a virtue.' Beat: mentor's challenge.

chapters.title: Counter-Memoir
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Writing the anti-Vivian chapters, Jonah realizes the family narrative he's defending is built on his grandfather's cruelty. His duty curdles. Beat: disillusionment with inheritance.

chapters.title: Midnight Archive
chapters.summary: August's POV. Caught after hours in the restricted collection by Jonah, she lies badly about why she's there. Trust cracks; he suspects she's working against him. Beat: secrecy breeding conflict.

chapters.title: The Argument in the Stairwell
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Their first real fight in ten years—all the accumulated accusations surface: who didn't show up, who stopped writing first. Both learn they were each given false information a decade ago. Beat: revelation reframes everything.

chapters.title: Who Kept the Letters
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He confronts his father, who admits intercepting August's letters all those years ago to protect the family name. Grief and fury. Beat: the villain revealed as banal duty.

chapters.title: Reconciliation in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: August's POV. Among winter-blooming camellias, they finally speak plainly—not yet the vow, but the truth of still loving each other. A kiss, then retreat. Beat: hope with trembling hands.

chapters.title: Marcus Reads the File
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Discovering August's access to the Kestrel letters, Marcus threatens to expose her breach of NDA unless she hands over material to destroy Vivian's version. Beat: blackmail raises stakes.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: August's POV. Vivian is moved to hospice care in the east wing; the memoir must be finished within days. August writes through the nights, Jonah bringing her tea without being asked. Beat: quiet devotion.

chapters.title: The Sentence Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Alone, Jonah finally drafts the sentence he's carried for a decade—I loved you then, I love you now, duty be damned—and can't yet say it aloud. Beat: the theme stated, withheld.

chapters.title: Betrayal Framed
chapters.summary: Marcus plants evidence that August leaked the letters to Jonah, turning Vivian's family against her and getting her locked out of the archive. Beat: darkest hour begins.

chapters.title: Locked Out
chapters.summary: August's POV. Barred from finishing the memoir, stripped of purpose, August decides to leave on the morning plow. She leaves behind her unpublished novel where Jonah will find it. Beat: surrender as gambit.

chapters.title: Reading Her Heart
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He finds the manuscript and reads the unfinished reunion scene—with a blank page left where his answer should go. He understands the vow was always waiting on him. Beat: epiphany.

chapters.title: Vivian's Last Chapter
chapters.summary: August's POV. Summoned to hospice, Vivian dictates her final pages herself: forgiveness for everyone, including the Kestrels, and releases August from the NDA. 'Say your sentence, child. Time is already running out—for all of us.' Beat: blessing and urgency.

chapters.title: The Plow Comes Early
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Roads clear; departure looms. Marcus moves to finalize the estate sale based on his fabricated narrative. Everything August and Jonah value ends at dawn. Beat: ticking clock maximal.

chapters.title: Breaking the Contract
chapters.summary: August's POV. August chooses ruin: she publicly declares the memoir's existence and its contents' truth at the family assembly, sacrificing her career and anonymity in one speech. Beat: courage over safety.

chapters.title: Jonah's Answer
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Before the assembled families, Jonah reads aloud the letter his father suppressed, then says the rehearsed sentence to August in front of everyone. Beat: climax—the vow spoken at last.

chapters.title: Marcus's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Confronted with his forgeries by Vivian's lawyer, Marcus collapses into confession; the estate's true history stands. He leaves in disgrace but not destroyed. Beat: antagonist resolved with mercy.

chapters.title: Last Light in the East Wing
chapters.summary: August's POV. Vivian dies at sunset holding both writers' hands, having heard her story told truly. Grief braided with peace. Beat: mourning as completion.

chapters.title: Bylines
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Months later: the dual memoirs publish side by side—hers under her own name for the first time, his rewritten as reconciliation rather than rebuttal. Reviews call them 'a conversation across a feud.' Beat: rebirth of vocation.

chapters.title: The Boathouse, Repaired
chapters.summary: August's POV. Spring. They restore the boathouse together and hold the ceremony they postponed a decade ago—private, unvowed in form, vowed in fact. Beat: the past tense becomes present.

chapters.title: Her Own Voice
chapters.summary: August's POV. At her first solo reading, August abandons her prepared text and tells the audience the true story of the snowstorm instead. Jonah watches from the back row. Beat: invisibility abandoned forever.

chapters.title: Letters Forwarded
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah's father, ill and contrite, returns the box of intercepted letters unopened. Jonah and August read them together, laughing and weeping, then burn what needs burning. Beat: inheritance transformed into choice.

chapters.title: Kestrel and the Vow
chapters.summary: Dual POV closing on shared narration. One year later, snow falling again on Ashcombe, now a writers' retreat in Vivian's name. August begins a new book; Jonah adds the final line to hers. Beat: love and memory reconciled; the vow kept, ongoing.
